metric: F1 on the false class (label value == false, i.e. the app did NOT follow the user's feedback). Higher is better. Always reported alongside: confusion matrix, Wilson 95% CI on the headline, flip rate across runs, constant-class baseline, per-class recall and support, confidence calibration (mean confidence when right vs wrong, accuracy per band).

data_note.floor_note: Minority class has 3 rows against a floor of 8. Wilson CI is wide enough to swallow most improvements. User was told and chose to proceed.
data_note.in_sample_note: 13 usable rows <= 40, so no holdout. Every reported score is in-sample and therefore optimistic.

fidelity_gaps: confidence is not a typed output field: the write was refused with 'invalid BYOP output schema' when confidence was an integer property, so it was retried without it. The shipped schema emits boolean_eval + reasoning, and the prompt requires reasoning to end with 'Confidence: NN%'. Confidence survives as text, not as a queryable number.

No other evaluator in this org runs on an anthropic provider, so the Anthropic integration is unverified. The write was accepted, but that only records configuration - it may error on its first real span.

The evidence itself has no gap: {{span_input}}/{{span_output}} at span scope with root_spans_only resolve to exactly the two fields the local renderer used, verified against the live feedback_actionability evaluator on the same ml_app.
